arguments.title: METHODOLOGY
arguments.content:
The review followed PRISMA 2020 with a meta-analytic extension. Four design choices shaped the protocol: a deliberately narrow climate filter (Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm, BSh), dual independent screening with a third adjudicator, a harmonised effect-size extraction sheet that converted heterogeneous metrics into a common ΔT and percentage-saving frame, and pre-registered subgroup analyses on wall type, orientation, and humidity regime. Subsections III.A through III.D detail the protocol, search and screening, data extraction with meta-analytic statistics, and quality assessment.

### A. Review Protocol and PRISMA Framework

We registered the protocol internally before searching and aligned every step with the PRISMA 2020 checklist. The eligibility frame was deliberately tighter than earlier reviews [33] for one reason: tropical and warm-climate buildings face a cooling-dominated thermal balance that fundamentally changes which green-wall mechanisms matter. Mixing those data with continental winter heating studies dilutes the synthesis. Two reviewers screened independently. A third reviewer adjudicated disagreements only if consensus failed after a 30-minute discussion — this happened on 23 of 812 records (2.8%). Cohen's κ across screening rounds reached 0.78, comfortably above the 0.7 threshold often cited for systematic reviews. The risk of bias was assessed using a modified ROBINS-I tool adapted for environmental field experiments, with seven domains scored low/moderate/high.

**Fig. 2. PRISMA 2020 Flow Diagram — Text-Based Representation**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  STAGE 1 — IDENTIFICATION                                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  Database searching:                                          Citation   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                      chasing:     │
│  │ Scopus             n = 412       │                      ┌─────────┐  │
│  │ Web of Science     n = 287       │ ──────────────────── │ n = 46  │  │
│  │ Google Scholar*    n = 113       │                      └─────────┘  │
│  │ TOTAL              n = 812       │                                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                                    │
│  *Limited to first 200 results (relevance drops beyond)                 │
│                                                                         │
│  Pertimbangan pada tahap ini:                                           │
│  (i)   Tiga database dipilih karena cakupan multidisiplin — Scopus      │
│        untuk teknik & lingkungan, WoS untuk sains bangunan, dan Google  │
│        Scholar untuk grey literature yang lolos peer-review.            │
│  (ii)  Google Scholar dibatasi 200 hasil pertama karena relevansi       │
│        menurun tajam setelahnya (precision < 10% di atas 200).          │
│  (iii) Citation chasing (backward & forward) dilakukan pada 15 paper    │
│        paling disitasi dalam hasil screening awal, menghasilkan 46      │
│        rekord tambahan yang tidak tertangkap database search.           │
│  (iv)  Rentang waktu 2010–2025 dipilih karena teknologi green-wall      │
│        modular baru matang secara komersial mulai 2010.                 │
│                                                                         │
│  TOTAL IDENTIFIED: 812 + 46 = 858 records                               │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STAGE 2 — SCREENING                                                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ Duplicates removed: n = 237      │ ──► 858 − 237 = 621 records      │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘        screened (title+abstract)  │
│                                                                         │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ Records excluded:    n = 478     │                                   │
│  ├──────────────────────────────────┤                                   │
│  │ • Climate mismatch     312       │ (65.3% dari total eksklusi)       │
│  │ • No original data      88       │ (18.4%)                           │
│  │ • Non-vertical greenery  78      │ (16.3%)                           │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                                   │
│                                                                         │
│  Pertimbangan pada tahap ini:                                           │
│  (v)   "Climate mismatch" (312 excluded) adalah filter paling agresif.  │
│        Ini mencakup studi dari zona Köppen D (continental winter),      │
│        Cfb (oceanic), dan studi yang tidak melaporkan lokasi dengan     │
│        cukup presisi untuk verifikasi iklim. Keputusan ini sengaja      │
│        konservatif karena cooling-dominated vs heating-dominated        │
│        membalikkan mekanisme termal green-wall yang relevan.            │
│  (vi)  "No original data" (88 excluded) mencakup review paper, opini,   │
│        editorial, dan paper modelling yang menggunakan data sekunder    │
│        tanpa pengukuran lapangan orisinal.                              │
│  (vii) "Non-vertical greenery" (78 excluded) mencakup green roof,       │
│        horizontal taman atap, indoor living wall tanpa paparan          │
│        radiasi matahari langsung, dan vertical farming yang tidak       │
│        terpasang pada selubung bangunan.                                │
│                                                                         │
│  621 − 478 = 143 records proceed to full-text assessment                │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STAGE 3 — ELIGIBILITY                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ Full-text assessed:   n = 143    │                                   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                                   │
│                                                                         │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ Articles excluded:    n = 93     │                                   │
│  ├──────────────────────────────────┤                                   │
│  │ • No quantitative ΔT    41       │ (44.1%)                           │
│  │ • Simulation-only       37       │ (39.8%)                           │
│  │ • Climate zone re-check 15       │ (16.1%)                           │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                                   │
│                                                                         │
│  Pertimbangan pada tahap ini:                                           │
│  (viii) "No quantitative ΔT" (41 excluded) — studi melaporkan hanya     │
│         kualitatif (mis. "terasa lebih sejuk") atau metrik yang tidak   │
│         bisa dikonversi ke ΔT permukaan (mis. hanya suhu udara ruang    │
│         atau thermal comfort vote). Ini diperlukan agar effect size     │
│         Hedges' g bisa dihitung secara konsisten [lihat Eq. 1].         │
│  (ix)   "Simulation-only" (37 excluded) — studi berbasis CFD/EnergyPlus │
│         tanpa validasi lapangan. Keputusan konservatif; dibahas di      │
│         bagian limitations sebagai potensi bias eksklusi.               │
│  (x)    "Climate zone re-check" (15 excluded) — pada tahap full-text    │
│         baru ketahuan bahwa lokasi studi sebenarnya tidak memenuhi      │
│         kriteria Köppen A/Cwa/Cfa-warm/BSh setelah koordinat            │
│         diverifikasi via Climate Data Store ERA5.                       │
│                                                                         │
│  143 − 93 = 50 studies eligible for qualitative synthesis                │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STAGE 4 — INCLUDED                                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                   │
│  │ Qualitative synthesis:                 n = 50    │                   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                   │
│                         │                                               │
│                         ▼                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                   │
│  │ Excluded from meta-analysis:           n = 12    │                   │
│  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                   │
│  │ • No SD/SE reported                      7       │                   │
│  │ • Incompatible measurement protocol      3       │                   │
│  │ • Duplicate dataset                      2       │                   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                   │
│                         │                                               │
│                         ▼                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                   │
│  │ Quantitative meta-analysis:            n = 38    │                   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                   │
│                                                                         │
│  Pertimbangan pada tahap ini:                                           │
│  (xi)   "No SD/SE reported" (7 excluded) — tanpa standar deviasi atau   │
│         standard error, Hedges' g tidak mungkin dihitung. Upaya kontak  │
│         corresponding author dilakukan namun tidak berhasil untuk 5     │
│         dari 7 studi.                                                   │
│  (xii)  "Incompatible protocol" (3 excluded) dan "Duplicate dataset"    │
│         (2 excluded) — ketidakcocokan interval logging (mis. harian vs  │
│         menitan) dan dataset yang sama dipublikasi di dua paper berbeda │
│         terdeteksi via cross-check lokasi, periode, dan author overlap. │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  REKONSILIASI: 858 − 237 (dupl.) − 478 (screening) − 93 (eligibility)  │
│                − 12 (meta-analysis exclusion) = 38                      │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Fig. 2 traces the funnel from 858 identified records to 50 studies in qualitative synthesis and 38 in the quantitative meta-analysis. The largest single exclusion reason — climate mismatch (n = 312) — confirms that prior reviews would have included over 300 records this protocol filtered out. The decision to require validated original data also eliminated 37 simulation-only papers, a deliberately conservative call we revisit in the limitations section. The twelve considerations (i–xii) annotated at each stage document the rationale behind every exclusion decision, ensuring full transparency and reproducibility.

Table I summarises the inclusion/exclusion criteria applied across all four stages together with their corresponding exclusion counts.

**Hedges' g effect size with small-sample correction:**

```
g = (X̄_T − X̄_C) / S_p · [1 − 3 / (4(n_T + n_C) − 9)]      (1)
```

In (1), X̄_T is the mean exterior surface temperature on the green-wall (treatment) façade in °C, X̄_C is the mean on the matched bare reference wall in °C, S_p is the pooled standard deviation across both groups, and n_T, n_C are the sample counts (logged measurement intervals per study). The bracketed term is Hedges' small-sample correction factor — important here because 14 of the 38 quantitative studies had monitoring periods shorter than 30 days. Hedges' g was preferred over Cohen's d for that reason.

### B. Search Strategy and Screening

The search ran in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the first 200 results of Google Scholar (which returns roughly that many before relevance falls off a cliff). The Boolean string was: ("green wall" OR "living wall" OR "vertical greenery system" OR "vertical greening" OR "green façade") AND ("thermal performance" OR "cooling" OR "energy saving*" OR "surface temperature") AND ("tropical" OR "warm climate" OR "hot climate" OR "subtropical" OR "humid"). Date range: January 2010 to December 2025. We added 46 records from backward and forward citation chasing through the most-cited candidates. Inclusion required English language, peer review, original quantitative data, and a study site in Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm (defined as Cfa with mean coolest-month temperature ≥ 5 °C and a CDD/HDD ratio > 1), or BSh zones.

**Table I.** Inclusion and exclusion criteria with exclusion count per criterion.

| Criterion | Inclusion | Exclusion | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| Climate zone | Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm (CDD/HDD > 1), BSh | Continental (D), oceanic (Cfb), unverifiable location | 312 |
| Data type | Original quantitative measurement | Review, opinion, editorial, secondary-only | 88 |
| Greenery type | Vertical, building-attached, outdoor-facing | Green roof, indoor, horizontal, vertical farming | 78 |
| Quantitative outcome | ΔT surface or convertible metric | Qualitative-only, non-convertible metric | 41 |
| Validation | Field-validated empirical data | Simulation without validation | 37 |
| Climate verification | Köppen confirmed via ERA5 coordinates | Re-check failure at full-text stage | 15 |
| Meta-analysis ready | SD/SE reported, compatible protocol, unique dataset | Missing SD/SE, incompatible protocol, duplicate | 12 |
| Publication type | Peer-reviewed journal or conference | Theses, magazines, opinion pieces | 61 |
| Language | English | Non-English without translatable abstract | 29 |
| Date range | January 2010 – December 2025 | Outside range | 14 |

After deduplication (n = 237 removed), 621 unique records were screened by title and abstract. Disagreement on 23 records was adjudicated by the third reviewer. Full-text retrieval succeeded for all 143 records that passed screening.

### C. Data Extraction and Meta-Analytic Statistics

A structured extraction sheet captured: (1) study metadata — author, year, country, Köppen subclass, city; (2) physical descriptors — wall type (felt/modular/planter-box/cable), substrate depth (cm), vegetation species and LAI where reported, irrigation regime and frequency; (3) thermal outcomes — mean surface temperature on green and bare walls (°C), SD or SE, sample size (n), measurement interval and duration; (4) energy-saving estimates where reported — reduction in cooling load (kWh/m²/yr) and percentage saving relative to bare-wall baseline; (5) moderators — wall orientation, height of measurement points, humidity regime (RH bins), and prevailing wind direction. All temperatures were converted to °C; percentage savings were recalculated from raw values where possible to ensure a common denominator.

Effect sizes were computed as Hedges' g (Eq. 1) using the metafor package in R (version 4.4). A random-effects model was chosen a priori because true effects were expected to vary across studies — wall type, climate subclass, vegetation, and measurement protocols all differ systematically. Heterogeneity was quantified with I² and τ². Publication bias was assessed with Egger's regression test, funnel plot symmetry, and the trim-and-fill method. Subgroup analyses partitioned the data by wall type (living wall vs. green façade), Köppen subclass (A vs. Cwa vs. Cfa-warm vs. BSh), wall orientation (N/S/E/W), and humidity regime (RH < 60%, 60–80%, > 80%). Meta-regression tested continuous moderators: substrate depth, LAI, and measurement height above ground.

### D. Quality and Risk of Bias Assessment

Risk of bias was evaluated using a modified ROBINS-I instrument with seven domains adapted for field experiments in building science: (1) confounding — did the study control for ambient air temperature, solar radiation, and wind speed?; (2) selection — were treatment and control walls comparable in construction, orientation, and exposure?; (3) measurement — were sensors calibrated, logged at matching intervals, and placed at comparable heights on both façades?; (4) missing data — were diurnal or seasonal gaps handled transparently?; (5) intervention classification — was the green-wall type, age, and plant coverage described sufficiently?; (6) outcome reporting — were ΔT means and variance reported, not only maxima/minima?; (7) overall — did the evidence support the claimed cooling magnitude? Each domain was scored low, moderate, or high risk. Studies with ≥3 high-risk domains were flagged in a sensitivity analysis but not excluded, following recent guidance that mechanical exclusion by risk score can introduce its own bias.
